literature_proposed.summary: Follows from a published bound, not formalised. For n >= k^2 an exception has no prime factor <= k, so C(n,k) is good and n >= g(k). Konyagin's g(k) >= exp(c (log k)^2) exceeds k^3 once log k > 3/c, so for all large k there is no exception with n < k^3, and K can be taken as the last k below that point. The constant c is not explicit in what I read, so a formal proof needs an explicit lower bound for g(k).
